input.question: What happens to non-perishable or preserved food after it has been stored for over 200 years?
input.ground_truth: Honey pretty much never goes bad. Bacteria and stuff cant survive in or on it, so honey left sitting in a tomb 6,000 years ago is just as safe to eat as honey harvested today. Although the dust wont be great for you and any toxic substances on the surface still fuck you up pretty good.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What happens to non-perishable or preserved food after it has been stored for over 200 years?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big jar of candy that’s been sitting in a special, dry, dark place for a *really* long time—like, longer than your great-great-great-grandparents have been alive! 

If the candy was packed very well and kept away from bugs, water, and air, it might still look okay, but it probably wouldn’t taste as yummy as when it was new. Some of the flavor and crunch might have gone away. Sometimes, it might even look a little funny or smell weird.

Most of the time, food that can last a long time (like canned beans or dried rice) can stay good for many years, but 200 years is a super long time! After that, it might not be safe to eat, or it might just taste old and not taste good anymore.

So, if you found a can of food that old, it’s better not to eat it, because it might make you sick or just taste really bad!
